prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1146; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received from the insured's driver reporting a collision while turning left at an intersection. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reports neck pain following the impact.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates coverage.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Officers and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact, and the other driver's account matches the description given to us.

Entry 4: Scene photographs and the witness statements are consistent with how the accident was described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair history provided.

Entry 5: Claimant was contacted by phone and gave the same account of the collision as in the initial report, including the sequence of the turn and the point of impact.

Entry 6: Medical records show a whiplash-type injury, which is a plausible result for a collision of this kind. The records also note a minor strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully with no lasting effects.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering as the claimant improved. Discharge notes describe steady recovery.

Entry 8: Repair estimate reviewed. Some of the listed damage may not be attributable to this impact, and it is not yet clear whether all of it resulted from this collision. Requested a supplemental inspection to separate the areas.

Entry 9: Claimant again gave a consistent account during a follow-up call. File referred for evaluation of the injury claim and the remaining vehicle damage items.
